claims.old: The framework simulates hybrid causal systems.
claims.new: The framework simulates hybrid causal systems (D-001, D-002).

claims.old: Such a system has five parts.
claims.new: Such a system has five parts.

claims.old: - Continuous dynamics. $\dot{x} = f(x, m, u, t)$ with algebraic outputs.
claims.new: - Continuous dynamics. $\dot{x} = f(x, m, u, t)$ with algebraic outputs.

claims.old: - Multi-rate periodic discrete dynamics. $s^{+} = g(s, u, t)$ at declared rates, with outputs held zero-order between ticks.
claims.new: - Multi-rate periodic discrete dynamics. $s^{+} = g(s, u, t)$ at declared rates, with outputs held zero-order between ticks (D-019)

claims.old: - Zero-crossing events. Guard functions with handlers, under two detection policies, stated below.
claims.new: - Zero-crossing events. Guard functions (each defining an event's predicate) with handlers, under two detection policies.

claims.old: - Post-step manifold projection. An optional per-component hook `x ← x_projection(x)`,
claims.new: - Post-step manifold projection. The formalism includes an optional per-component hook, `x ← x_projection(x)` (D-001).

claims.old: applied after each accepted step.
claims.new: It is applied after each accepted step and after any handler reset of `x` (§5.3).

claims.old: It covers quaternion renormalization, DCM orthonormalization and any other manifold-valued state.
claims.new: It covers quaternion renormalization, direction cosine matrix (DCM) orthonormalization and any other manifold-valued state.

claims.old: It is the cheap end of the projection-methods family from geometric integration.
claims.new: It is the cheap end of the projection-methods family from geometric integration.

claims.old: - External inputs. The runtime injects them asynchronously, from pilot controls or the network, under the staging rules of §11.
claims.new: - External inputs. The runtime injects them asynchronously, from pilot controls or the network, under the staging rules of §11 (D-022).

claims.old: ### 2.1 Events: two detection policies
claims.new: ### 2.1 Events: two detection policies

claims.old: Both policies share one declaration, a guard function plus a handler.
claims.new: Both policies share one declaration, a guard function plus a handler (D-179).

claims.old: Only detection differs.
claims.new: Only detection differs.

claims.old: - Boundary-detected (cheap). The framework checks each guard for a not-holding → holding edge against its prior (§10.6) at step boundaries only.
claims.new: - Boundary-detected (cheap). The framework checks each guard for a not-holding → holding edge against its prior (§10.6) at step boundaries only.

claims.old: There is no root-finding and no step rejection.
claims.new: There is no root-finding and no step rejection.

claims.old: The handler fires at the end of the step in which the edge was observed.
claims.new: The handler fires at the end of the step in which the edge was observed.

claims.old: The cost is one guard evaluation per event per step.
claims.new: The cost is one guard evaluation per event per round of the boundary's event iteration (§10.6).

claims.old: This policy is fully compatible with fixed-step real-time execution.
claims.new: This policy is fully compatible with fixed-step real-time execution.

claims.old: - Localized (precise). The framework finds the crossing instant by root-finding.
claims.new: - Localized (precise). The framework finds the crossing instant by root-finding (D-018).

claims.old: This policy serves events where timing precision genuinely matters.
claims.new: This policy serves events where timing precision genuinely matters.

claims.old: §10.4 gives the mechanics.
claims.new: §10.4 gives the mechanics.

claims.old: Detection policy never depends on real-time pacing (§10.7).
claims.new: Detection policy never depends on real-time pacing (§10.7, D-080).

claims.old: Time events and state events. The discrete tier's ticks, declared by `sample_times`, are time events.
claims.new: The discrete tier's ticks are time events (D-220).

claims.old: declared by `sample_times`,
claims.new: Ticks are declared by `sample_times`.

claims.old: Their instants are known in advance and scheduled (§10.5).
claims.new: Their instants are known in advance and scheduled (§10.5).

claims.old: Everything declared through `StateEvent(guard, handler)` is a state event.
claims.new: Everything declared through `StateEvent(guard, handler)` is a state event.

claims.old: Its instant is unknown and must be detected, by boundary check or by localization.
claims.new: Its instant is unknown and must be detected, by boundary check or by localization.

claims.old: That is why the declaration is named `state_events` (§8.2).
claims.new: That is why the declaration is named `state_events` (§8.2, D-220).

claims.old: The criterion is detection versus scheduling, not which fields a guard reads.
claims.new: The criterion is detection versus scheduling, not which fields a guard reads.

claims.old: A guard over an input is still a state event.
claims.new: A guard over an input is still a state event.

claims.old: This arrangement gives step-boundary logic well-defined semantics.
claims.new: The two-policy arrangement gives step-boundary logic well-defined semantics.

claims.old: The crossing defines the transition.
claims.new: The crossing defines the transition (D-179).

claims.old: Detection resolution is an execution-policy detail.
claims.new: Detection resolution is an execution-policy detail.

claims.old: A guard defines a predicate.
claims.new: A guard defines a predicate (D-082, D-001).

claims.old: It does so in one of two forms, either a `Bool`-valued form or the sign of a continuous function under the normative convention positive = predicate holds.
claims.new: It does so in one of two forms, either a `Bool`-valued form or the sign of a continuous function under the normative convention positive = predicate holds.

claims.old: Writing the guard's sign value `σ`, holding means `σ ≥ 0`.
claims.new: Writing the guard's sign value `σ`, holding means `σ ≥ 0`.

claims.old: An event fires when its predicate transitions from not-holding to holding.
claims.new: An event fires when its predicate transitions from not-holding to holding (D-082, D-001).

claims.old: This is edge semantics, and it is uniform across both forms.
claims.new: This is edge semantics, and it is uniform across both forms.

claims.old: §10.6 states the prior bookkeeping.
claims.new: §10.6 states the bookkeeping of the prior. The prior is each event's predicate sample stored at the previous boundary (a published consistency point).

claims.old: The opposite crossing direction is declared as a second event with the negated guard.
claims.new: The opposite crossing direction is declared as a second event with the negated guard (D-082).

claims.old: Stall entry and exit are one such pair.
claims.new: Stall entry and exit are one such pair.

claims.old: Which form an author declares is not a free choice.
claims.new: Which form an author declares is not a free choice.

claims.old: The guard's return type is the declared policy.
claims.new: The guard's return type is the declared policy.

claims.old: A `Bool` return declares boundary-detected, and the sign form declares localized (D-179).
claims.new: A `Bool` return declares boundary-detected, and the sign form declares localized (D-179).

claims.old: §10.4 states the rule, the exactness result that motivates the `Bool` form, and the gate idiom for localizing mixed predicates.
claims.new: §10.4 states the rule, the exactness result that motivates the `Bool` form, and the gate idiom for localizing mixed predicates.

claims.old: ### 2.2 Exclusions (deliberate)
claims.new: ### 2.2 Exclusions (deliberate)

claims.old: - No DAEs / algebraic constraints.
claims.new: - No differential-algebraic equations (DAEs) or algebraic constraints.

claims.old: The actual need is state manifolds, and projection covers it (D-001).
claims.new: The actual need is state manifolds, and projection, the optional per-component hook `x ← x_projection(x)`, covers it (D-001).

claims.old: - No SDEs / stochastic integrators.
claims.new: - No stochastic differential equations (SDEs) or stochastic integrators.

claims.old: Noise processes such as Dryden/von Kármán turbulence and sensor noise are modeled as ordinary RNG-driven discrete processes, that is, shaping filters.
claims.new: Noise processes, such as sensor noise and Dryden/von Kármán turbulence, are modeled as shaping filters (D-001), that is, as ordinary discrete processes driven by a random number generator (RNG).

claims.old: That modeling is faithful to how they are specified, and it is cheap.
claims.new: That modeling is faithful to how the noise processes are specified, and it is cheap.

claims.old: One consequence is elevated to a framework guarantee, deterministic replay.
claims.new: One consequence is elevated to a framework guarantee, deterministic replay

claims.old: RNG state lives in component discrete state (`s`), never in ambient globals, so the same seed gives a bit-identical trajectory.
claims.new: RNG state lives in component discrete state `s`, never in ambient globals, so the same seed gives a bit-identical trajectory (D-231).

claims.old: - No unconditional per-step hook, so no `f_step!` equivalent.
claims.new: So there is no equivalent of `f_step!`, FlightCore's per-step hook.

claims.old: - No unconditional per-step hook,
claims.new: - No unconditional per-step hook, because its semantics depend on the step size (D-001).

claims.old: Every current use decomposes into one of two mechanisms.
claims.new: Every current use of `f_step!` decomposes into one of two mechanisms.

claims.old: Projection covers quaternion renormalization.
claims.new: Projection covers quaternion renormalization.

claims.old: Boundary-detected events (checked for edges at step boundaries only, no root-finding) cover engine phase transitions and the stall hysteresis latch.
claims.new: Boundary-detected events (checked for edges at step boundaries only, no root-finding) cover engine phase transitions and the stall hysteresis latch.

claims.old: For one class the mapping tightens semantics.
claims.new: For one group of uses the mapping tightens semantics.

claims.old: Level-triggered cross-component resets become edge-triggered events.
claims.new: Level-triggered cross-component resets become edge-triggered events.

claims.old: The gear friction regulator under `!wow` is one such reset (§5.3, D-001).
claims.new: Flight.jl resets the gear's friction regulator while `!wow` (no weight on wheels) holds; here that reset becomes an event on the touchdown edge (§5.3, D-001, D-141).
